bugs.summary: The refactor replaced the Accept-Encoding match with `options?.encoding ?? ENCODING_TYPES.find(...)`. When the `encoding` option is set, `??` short-circuits and the request's Accept-Encoding header is never consulted, so the middleware compresses every response with that encoding regardless of what the client accepts. A client that advertises only deflate, or sends no Accept-Encoding at all, still receives a gzip body labelled `Content-Encoding: gzip` and cannot decode it.
bugs.trigger: Mount `compress({ encoding: 'gzip' })`, return any response with a body, and request it with `Accept-Encoding: deflate` (or without that header): the response still carries `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Before this commit the same request was returned uncompressed. The fix (#4951) adds `selectEncoding()`, which parses Accept-Encoding (q-values, wildcard, case) even when an encoding is configured; its regression test expects no Content-Encoding when the configured encoding is not accepted.
